intro: Lesson 15: The Greek legacy: from Baghdad to our high streets. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Keeping knowledge alive
points: Kept and studied in the Muslim world

timeline.label: 1100s AD
timeline.text: Arabic works translated into Latin in Toledo, Spain

model.title: Is the British Museum front Greek-style?

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Yes: columns and a pediment copy Greek temples

keywords.def: something left behind for the future
a great library and centre of learning in Baghdad
a building style copying ancient Greek and Roman designs

questions.q: Explain how a Greek medical book reached Europe.
questions.a: Written in Greek, translated into Arabic in Baghdad, studied and added to, then translated into Latin

questions.q: Core: In the portal response box, write a short explanation: 'How did Greek ideas reach us?' using the four steps. Starter: 'Greek ideas reached us because ...'
questions.a: Four steps with Baghdad and Muslim scholars named

questions.q: Extend: Find one Greek-style building in Britain online and label its columns and pediment.
Stretch: Why does it matter that Muslim scholars added new ideas, not just copied?
questions.a: Knowledge grew: they corrected mistakes and made new discoveries

questions.q: Where were many Greek books translated into Arabic?
questions.a: A) Baghdad. In the House of Wisdom in Baghdad under the Abbasids.

questions.q: Big question: how did Greek books survive?
questions.a: They were copied, translated into Arabic and studied by Muslim scholars, then passed to Europe
